q: She doesn’t have anything prepared yet, and I want to help her get set up in a practical way. I want to plan a baby shower for essentials, but I know there’s more to think about. I’d really appreciate advice on what she actually needs for a newborn, what we should be prioritizing first (like medical care and basic needs), any helpful programs or resources in PA.
cx: An older sister helps a young sister who found out at 21 weeks; parents took it badly.

q: He admitted, “I’m scared of messing him up.” That hit me hard, but it also made sense.
cx: At 27 weeks with a third child, her husband has gone distant since learning it's a boy. Post reads polished.

q: He doesn’t have any close family, and neither do I. We live in a rural area, we don’t have a lot of friends around us that we’re close to either.
cx: Due mid-July with two daughters at home and no one nearby to lean on.

q: My husband seems to think his role is to support me TO get an epidural. He gave me the whole spiel about how we're not living in the dark ages, I won't get a medal, all of that stuff.
cx: US first-time mother wants to try labour without medication first; husband pushes the other way.

q: We're in a birthing class through the hospital right now and we just covered comfort techniques. The class before was about medical interventions (including pain meds). I think the topic is top of mind for him right now, so he is trying to figure out more specific things to do or say.
cx: How the hospital class shaped her husband's ideas of his role.

q: I have been reading a lot about hypnobirthing and I feel mentally ready to try for this.
cx: Her own preparation alongside a hospital birthing class.

q: instead of bringing a gift for my new niece since I’ve already purchased her several things and plan on doing for her for the rest of her life, I want to bring a gift for my little sister to the baby shower instead. Do yall have any suggestions?
cx: A big sister wants a shower gift for the mother rather than the baby.

q: Then after baby was here and things had calmed down he just kept leaving. To go outside, to go make a call, to go get food, he even left for 3 hours to go to a softball tournament he was supposed to be coaching had baby not came that weekend.
cx: After a hard birth she resents how her husband spent the hospital stay; his mother came though she wanted no one.

q: He sleeps through most of the night feeds but is helpful during the day. Only other complaint is he invited a ton of people over the day we came home which was super overwhelming for me.
cx: First days home with a newborn.

q: I laid down for one second and fell asleep for an hour. I awoke to my wife stressed out like crazy telling me I was no help that night
cx: A new father's first night in the postpartum room after an early birth.

q: Im just going from super happy and excited to so scared that I’m not doing anything right to overwhelmed when a family member comes and gives baby advice I honestly just wanna hear from the nurses and doctors, like there’s so many things at once.
cx: Asking if this swing of feelings is what birth is like for everyone.

q: expected me to be in a good mood and use a right tone of voice
cx: Her mother arrived to help after the birth and then criticised her for a week.

q: I now have trouble moving forward and not feeling fearful of other guest, even though logically I know they will be more helpful/nice :(
cx: After her mother's visit went badly, she dreads the next visitors.

q: We explained upon entering that there are some rules, no kissing on the face, head and hands. Of course 10 minutes in the boundaries were violated. Both of us too tired to react in time, realised only when it was too late.
cx: A father recalls a neighbour's first visit a few weeks after the birth.

q: Wife was trying to tell her that it’s the last thing we need help with, and we would appreciate way more if someone would walk the dogs or make groceries
cx: The neighbour keeps asking to come and hold the baby.

q: I don’t know if that’s because I didn’t do skin to skin, the midwife insisted on bundling him up before handing him to me. Or because there wasn’t a family room, so I wasn’t able to stay in the hospital and had to leave after 30 minutes with the two of them alone.
cx: A father the night after the birth wonders why he hasn't felt it click yet.

q: Then my sister keeps going on about how awful birth is going to be and how miserable I’ll feel in the third trimester. Like all the time. At least twice a day she mentions it.
cx: UK, easy pregnancy so far; mother and sister flood her with warnings and rules.

q: I know pregnancy and birth aren’t easy, I’m but I don’t think constantly hearing negative things is helping at all.
cx: She wants the horror stories to stop, not more of them.

q: My mum also keeps saying I need to get married before the third trimester as I don’t want to look back at my wedding pictures years later and see myself fat and swollen.
cx: Her mother's pressure alongside a no-caffeine rule.
